extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, PIs, administrators, and institutional staff
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy, process, and resource updates intended to inform grant applicants and the research community about changes and guidance affecting applications, review, and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 application format and linked-award handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Know key features and the application format for the Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) award and that applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and awardees should embed replication and reproducibility throughout NIH-funded research to ensure reliability and public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise."

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' score
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Competitive but not discussed’ denotes applications falling in the middle third of a study section following emergency review modifications; strong applications can be designated this way if they fall below a 33% cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Last November, NIH implemented emergency modifications to review processes following resumption of activities after the lapse in appropriations. Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of peer review (CSR) goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralizing peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in NIH peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... As the one-year anniversary approaches, we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
